aws::graph::propositions: Taiwan manufactures 90 percent of the world's advanced microchips.
The world's dependence on Taiwan's chips has protected Taiwan from a potential invasion or trade sanctions from China.
The United States produces 10 percent of the world's semiconductors.
China produces 5 percent of the world's semiconductors.
South Korea and Japan produce the remaining semiconductors.
All major U.S. defense systems and platforms rely on semiconductors for their performance.
The erosion of U.S. capabilities in microelectronics directly threatens the United States' ability to defend itself and its allies.
The CHIPS Act ensures that the U.S. semiconductor supply chain is secure and does not rely on countries like China.
The CHIPS Act is a long-term plan to promote research and development in the U.S. semiconductor industry.
Foundries located in the U.S. may still rely on cheap parts from Chinese companies that are sponsored by the Chinese government.
The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) implemented new restrictions in August that limit the ability of U.S. companies to sell certain semiconductor technologies to China.
